- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; if sentiment turns negative after a peak, delay forecast drop by 1–2 days and reduce slope.
- For 30-day horizon, model overfits recent volatility; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.1–0.2) and price is flat, model often overpredicts; apply 1–2% downward bias to avoid false breakout.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 0.3 → 0.1 → 0.3), model misreads momentum; use 2-day moving average of sentiment to guide forecast direction.
